summary: The tenant-isolation work is genuinely solid: orgId for both new /api/v1/reports/** routes comes exclusively from requireAuthOrApiKey()'s authenticated context, is never read from the request body/query, and this is verified by a real spoofing test plus a cross-org test; the routes are otherwise thin, well-tested wrappers around the existing executeReportDefinition()/getFullReportCatalog() dispatcher and withTenantContext()/RLS path already used at ~30 other call sites, and the new actorId/requireAuthOrApiKey pattern exactly matches the already-merged PROJEXA sibling route, so no new tenant-isolation or auth-bypass risk was found. However, this diff also introduces the codebase's first server-side CSV export endpoint (rowsToCSV in src/lib/report-export-shared.ts), reachable by design from external AI agents and reseller apps via a scoped API key, and it performs zero CSV/formula-injection sanitization: report rows routinely contain user-controlled free text pulled straight from the DB (vendor/supplier names, item names, AI-recipe-generated notes -- confirmed by reading report-engine-service.ts), so a value starting with '=', '+', '-', or '@' (e.g. a vendor name) flows unescaped into the CSV response and will be interpreted as a live formula by Excel/Sheets when a downstream human or agent opens the exported file -- a well-known, OWASP-documented class of vulnerability (CSV/formula injection), and a materially different risk profile than the internal-only exports this codebase has shipped so far given the entire point of this route is external consumption. The XLSX path is comparatively safer since XLSX.utils.json_to_sheet writes explicit string-typed cells, but the CSV path has no such protection. Given this is a tier1 diff whose approval means autonomous merge straight to main with no human gate, and the missing sanitization is a concrete, realistic, unaddressed security gap in a brand-new external-facing surface, this should not auto-merge as-is.
issues: rowsToCSV() in src/lib/report-export-shared.ts does not sanitize values that begin with =, +, -, or @, allowing CSV/formula injection: report rows can contain user-controlled free text (vendor/supplier names, item names, AI-recipe notes per report-engine-service.ts), and this route is specifically designed for external AI agents/resellers to consume via API key, so a planted formula in source data becomes a live formula when the exported CSV is opened downstream. Fix by prefixing cell values that start with =, +, -, @, or tab/CR with a safe character (e.g. a leading single quote or space) before joining, as is standard practice for this vulnerability class.

Minor inconsistency (non-blocking): GET /api/v1/reports/catalog returns 200 with an empty catalog array when ctx.orgId is null, while POST /api/v1/reports/definitions/[id]/run returns 400 'No organisation found' for the same condition -- not a security issue, just an inconsistent contract worth aligning.
